info.title: aimem hub API
info.description: The complete HTTP surface of an aimem hub (and of the local service, which serves the same mux over a unix socket without auth). Every route except the three public pages (/, /v1/status, /admin) requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; routes marked x-role admin additionally need an admin token (the env token, or a tokens.json entry with role admin). This spec documents the surface and its auth contract; request/response bodies are intentionally loose (JSON objects) - the store types in internal/store are the authority on field shapes. A parity test (openapi_test.go) fails CI when this file and the real route table disagree.

get.summary: List users, access groups, membership, grants, ordinary-token metadata and the last 100 administration audit events

200.description: Access snapshot; no secrets or token digests

get.summary: Inspect authenticated identity and current task-write permission for an optional project
get.description: Also available to ordinary user tokens. Ordinary tokens may additionally use the task routes and /mcp task tools; they are refused on every other non-public endpoint. Legacy writer/admin credentials retain their existing rights. With ?project=<id>, every credential also receives tasks_enabled: whether an admin has switched tasks on for that project (task mutations are refused with 403 otherwise).

200.description: Identity including ordinary token scope (user, project or read-only), task_write scope/grant eligibility, and separate tasks_enabled setting

401.description: Invalid, expired, revoked or disabled credential

get.summary: List a project's epics (OPEN unless include_retired=true)
get.description: Ordinary user tokens may call this route. An epic is the grouping above tasks that a release or milestone maps to.

post.summary: Create an epic
post.description: Body: title (required), objective, target, state (OPEN by default). Authorized like a task write in this project (ordinary user-scoped or matching project-scoped token with a current grant, or admin; tasks must be enabled). Retry keys travel in the Idempotency-Key header.

400.description: invalid content

403.description: not authorized or tasks not enabled

get.description: Ordinary user tokens may call this route.

put.summary: Replace an epic's fields under expected_revision; state RETIRED retires it
put.description: Authorized like a task write. A stale expected_revision returns 409 with the current epic. Retirement keeps existing task assignments and refuses new ones; ids are never reused.

409.description: revision conflict, current epic in the body

get.summary: The identity directory: id, kind, name and enabled of every user and group
get.description: Ordinary user tokens may call this route: it is what the task page labels assignees and comment authors with. Nothing else about an identity is returned (no tokens, grants or project lists); effective permissions stay in the access store.

get.summary: The project's selected process reference (repository, ref, commit, manifest)
get.description: Ordinary user tokens may call this route: the reference is what an agent needs to find the project's process documents and grants no access to the repository. 404 when nothing is selected; ?history=1 adds the retained earlier selections, newest first, and answers 200 even when nothing is selected now.

put.summary: Select or clear the project's process reference (admin)
put.description: Body: repo (https/ssh/git@ URL), commit (full 40-hex), manifest (relative path in the repository), optional ref (branch or tag for servers that refuse fetch-by-hash), and expected_commit — the commit currently selected, empty when none — or the write is refused with 409 and the current selection. {"clear":true,"expected_commit":...} clears. Every selection is retained in the project's history.

400.description: malformed selection

409.description: expected_commit does not match the current selection

get.summary: List task summaries of a project
get.description: Archived tasks are excluded unless include_archived=true. Pages default 20, max 100; pass next_cursor as after. Managed rows include a read-only coordination object with team_id and optional active attempt_id/state; standalone clients must skip them. Ordinary user tokens may call this route; writes are authorized per attempt against the task's owning project (user-scoped token or token issued for that project instance, plus a current grant), legacy writer tokens read only, admin tokens do everything.

400.description: Validation failure (bad cursor, limit or filter)

401.description: Invalid, expired, revoked or disabled credential

post.summary: Create a task in an existing ordinary project
post.description: Body is the editable content (title required; state defaults to BACKLOG; candidate_refs and evidence_refs are typed references {kind, ref, note?, scope?} with kind one of task, doc, record, commit, pr, ci, url, text — a bare string is refused with 400 since schema 13). Never creates a project. Ordinary user tokens may call this route; writes are authorized per attempt against the task's owning project (user-scoped token or token issued for that project instance, plus a current grant), legacy writer tokens read only, admin tokens do everything. Retry keys travel in the Idempotency-Key header.

403.description: Credential may not write tasks in this project

409.description: Revision conflict (body carries current), idempotency key reused with different input, or archived task

get.description: Current content, revision, owning project (resolved at read time, so a rename is reflected) and origin-relative links. An optional read-only coordination object contains team_id and, when reserved, attempt_id/state; standalone clients must skip managed tasks even between attempts. Ordinary user tokens may call this route; writes are authorized per attempt against the task's owning project (user-scoped token or token issued for that project instance, plus a current grant), legacy writer tokens read only, admin tokens do everything.

put.summary: Replace a task's editable fields under expected-revision CAS
put.description: Body is the full editable content plus expected_revision; omitted optional fields clear (candidate_refs and evidence_refs are typed references {kind, ref, note?, scope?} — a bare string is refused with 400 since schema 13). A stale revision answers 409 with the current task. Ordinary user tokens may call this route; writes are authorized per attempt against the task's owning project (user-scoped token or token issued for that project instance, plus a current grant), legacy writer tokens read only, admin tokens may update unmanaged tasks. Retry keys travel in the Idempotency-Key header. Managed tasks refuse generic update/archive with 409 managed_task, including admins and old update receipts. Tasks with an active reservation also refuse generic update/archive with 409, including admins and old update receipts; the response does not disclose the holder. Reservation transitions are not exposed through this route. The coordination projection is not editable content.

post.summary: identity.v1: issue a single-use proof receipt for a registered peer and challenge
post.description: Only a live user-scoped individual token (ordinary role) may call this. The receipt is returned once to that credential holder, is valid for at most 60 s and can be redeemed only by the named peer. The response is no-store; the receipt must never enter a model-visible tool result, transcript or log. Requires TLS terminated by this hub: plain HTTP, a TLS-terminating proxy and the unix socket are refused with tls_required, and forwarded headers never count. Not exposed as an MCP tool.

post.description: Only an aimem_peer_ credential for the path's service may call this; a peer credential reaches no other route. Idempotency-Key is k1_ plus the unpadded base64url SHA-256 of aicrew's request key. An identical retry returns the recorded result after rechecking the token. Requires TLS terminated by this hub: plain HTTP, a TLS-terminating proxy and the unix socket are refused with tls_required, and forwarded headers never count. Not exposed as an MCP tool.

post.description: Binds service_id, this hub, identity.redeem, an https introspection endpoint and a TLS trust binding (ca_dns naming the endpoint host, or spki_sha256). One active peer per hub. Audited. Registration grants no project access or enrollment authority. Requires TLS terminated by this hub: plain HTTP, a TLS-terminating proxy and the unix socket are refused with tls_required, and forwarded headers never count. Not exposed as an MCP tool.

post.summary: Check a peer's introspection end to end
post.description: Sends one identity.v1 introspection to the registered peer with a random handle that no session holds, and reports a fixed outcome: ok is true only for a verified inactive answer. Before any network call the peer must be the single enabled peer on this hub, its endpoint the https URL of /v1/crew/introspect with a valid TLS trust binding, and AIMEM_INTROSPECTION_TOKEN_FILE a private file holding the credential; otherwise the outcome names what is missing. One attempt, at most 2 s, no redirect or proxy. The answer never contains the credential or the handle. Audited with the outcome. Requires TLS terminated by this hub: plain HTTP, a TLS-terminating proxy and the unix socket are refused with tls_required, and forwarded headers never count. Not exposed as an MCP tool.

200.description: The check ran: {service_id, ok, outcome}. outcome is inactive (healthy) or one fixed reason: peer_disabled, peer_ambiguous, wrong_hub, peer_record, not_configured, credential_file, tls_untrusted, timeout, cancelled, transport, redirect, status, version_rejected, oversize, malformed, nonce_mismatch, wrong_service, bad_generation, expired, bad_role, unexpected_active

get.description: Admin audit page over an existing ordinary project with tasks enabled: accepted team events in sequence order after the cursor, with next_cursor; after (nonnegative sequence) and limit (1-100, default 50). Optional filters narrow the page: session_id (the event session, the assignment worker or either handoff side), task_id (assignment or managed task), attempt_id (assignment or managed attempt), operation (exact name or a prefix ending in a dot), since/until (RFC3339, half-open on the server timestamp; a fractional bound rounds up to the next whole second because stored timestamps are whole seconds, which keeps the half-open meaning). Unknown or repeated query parameters are refused. Records carry actor identity IDs (never token values), request ID, server and process versions; see /export for JSONL pages with messages.

get.description: Admin JSONL export page (application/x-ndjson) of a team's accepted events and message metadata for post-analysis; every page runs the admin gate again. Lines: one header record (schema_version 1, protocol_version, project, team_id, normalized filters, include_bodies, limit, snapshot {event_sequence, message_sequence, taken_at}, first_page, exported_at, server_version, request_id), then up to limit event records, then up to limit message records, then one end record (events, messages, complete, next {after_events, after_messages, snapshot_events, snapshot_messages}). The first page takes the snapshot; a continued page passes all four next values back so records accepted after the snapshot never appear; complete:true marks the last page. Message records are metadata by default: id, sequence, sender session and generation, reported profile as stored, created_at, recipient, kind, task/attempt/reply references, lifecycle record and one delivery record per recipient (delivered_at means an inbox response was served, acked_at is the client's explicit report); include_bodies=true adds the payload. Filters as on /events; an operation filter selects lifecycle messages by their operation. A stream whose snapshot sequence is zero yields nothing on any page. limit 1-100 (default 50). Nothing here infers model identity or cost; rotated server diagnostics are not part of the export.

post.summary: Team session join
post.description: Requires a live ordinary project write token and current team enrollment, including roster reads and retry replay. Admin/local/legacy/read-only credentials are refused. Protocol version 1. Join accepts exact team name or ID and role/profile; other operations require stable team ID, session_id and generation. Profile replacement also needs expected_profile_revision. Writes require Idempotency-Key and strict JSON at most 64 KiB. Roster uses session_id, generation, after and limit (1-100). Responses exclude internal user/token bindings. Workers wait for explicit assignment; messaging supports send/history/inbox/ack; assignment HTTP primitives exist, but the full execution/result/recovery workflow is not ready.
